newsitem.title: UK: London silver jumps to highest fix since Oct '96.
newsitem.headline: London silver jumps to highest fix since Oct '96.

text.p: Silver fixed at 497.25 cents per ounce on Friday, its highest fixing since October 24, 1996. It fixed on Thursday at 473.00 cents.
London silver jumps to highest fix since Oct'96
Increasing confidence that silver had largely survived any weakness from the gold price's fall since the beginning of the year encouraged mainly U.S.-based investment funds to buy the metal.

"Silver's move was justified somewhat but it is not convincing yet. Today it would have to close between $4.88 and $4.92 before there would be a good chance it could go further," a market analyst said.
Unlike gold, silver is largely an industrial metal which is mainly used in photography, jewellery and silverware and a variety of industrial applications.
"The major economies are doing well and there are no central bank sales in silver so there is no justification to sell the industrial metals just now," a silver market observer said.
However the silver market is notoriously volatile and a leading London-based dealer warned, "Silver is looking very dangerous, potentially very volatile."
